title: Public API — Open Circuit SF
description: Read-only JSON API for Open Circuit SF events and newsletter issues. No key needed; CORS enabled.

intro.text: A read-only JSON API for our events and newsletter issues. It needs no account or key, answers GET only, and sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * so a browser app on any site can read it. Successful responses are cacheable for 60 seconds. It serves the same operations as our
intro.tail: , and a route and its tool return the same JSON.

blocks.label: Base URL
blocks.text: https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/

items: limit defaults to 10 and is capped at 50.
Dates are RFC 3339 with an offset, or YYYY-MM-DD in America/Los_Angeles.
60 requests a minute per IP, one budget shared between /mcp and /api/public/v1/. Past that you get HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds.
List results may be cached on the server for up to 60 seconds.
Errors are JSON: {"error":{"code","message","fields"}}. Unknown, draft and unpublished items all return the same 404.

blocks.text: The OpenAPI document describes every endpoint:
List upcoming Open Circuit SF events, soonest first. Parameters: limit (default 10, max 50); after and before, each an RFC 3339 time or a YYYY-MM-DD date in America/Los_Angeles.

blocks.label: Example request
blocks.text: curl -s 'https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/events?limit=1'

blocks.label: Example response
blocks.text:
{
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "esp32-intro",
      "slug": "esp32-intro",
      "title": "Intro to ESP32",
      "summary": "Build and program your first ESP32 board.",
      "starts_at": "2026-12-05T13:00:00-08:00",
      "ends_at": "2026-12-05T16:00:00-08:00",
      "location_name": "Noisebridge",
      "address": "272 Capp St, San Francisco, CA",
      "status": "scheduled",
      "registration_url": "https://lu.ma/example",
      "url": "https://www.opencircuitsf.com/events/esp32-intro",
      "event_type": "workshop",
      "tags": [
        "microcontrollers"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Search Open Circuit SF events by words in the title, description and tags. Parameters: query (every word must match; cut to 200 characters; empty matches all); from and to (RFC 3339 or YYYY-MM-DD); include_past (default false); limit (default 10, max 50).

blocks.label: Example request
blocks.text: curl -s 'https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/events/search?query=esp32&limit=1'

blocks.label: Example response
blocks.text:
{
  "events": [
    {
      "id": "esp32-intro",
      "slug": "esp32-intro",
      "title": "Intro to ESP32",
      "summary": "Build and program your first ESP32 board.",
      "starts_at": "2026-12-05T13:00:00-08:00",
      "ends_at": "2026-12-05T16:00:00-08:00",
      "location_name": "Noisebridge",
      "address": "272 Capp St, San Francisco, CA",
      "status": "scheduled",
      "registration_url": "https://lu.ma/example",
      "url": "https://www.opencircuitsf.com/events/esp32-intro",
      "event_type": "workshop",
      "tags": [
        "microcontrollers"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Get one Open Circuit SF event by its id (its slug), from list_upcoming_events or search_events. Adds location_note and description to the list fields. An event whose slug is search cannot be read here, because events/search takes that path; use the MCP get_event tool for it.

blocks.label: Example request
blocks.text: curl -s 'https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/events/esp32-intro'

blocks.label: Example response

List Open Circuit SF newsletter issues, newest first. Parameter: limit (default 10, max 50).

blocks.label: Example request
blocks.text: curl -s 'https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/newsletter?limit=1'

blocks.label: Example response

blocks.text: Get one Open Circuit SF newsletter issue by its id (its slug), from list_newsletter_issues. Adds the body as plain text.

blocks.label: Example request
blocks.text: curl -s 'https://www.opencircuitsf.com/api/public/v1/newsletter/november-2026'

blocks.label: Example response
blocks.text:
{
